First ask whether the records can be compared at all; then look at the numbers.

Can these records actually be compared?

The comparison table sets the selected records side by side on definition, population or calculation base, period, method, source and currentness. Check geography and unit in each evidence record before comparing values. Terms such as accounts, active accounts, subscribers, beneficiaries, merchants and POS terminals may sound related but are not interchangeable. Material mismatches remain visible and prevent a false common scale or combined result.

Do not infer:

The same word does not mean the same measure. The comparison does not reconcile differing figures or prefer one number unless evidence on their definitions supports it.

Select at least two records.

No automatic averages · no preferred number · no invented conversion factor

02Analysis

Three measures that cannot be combined

Three kinds of figure are often set side by side. 11.9% is the share of adults (15+) in the survey's covered areas who had an account in the 2021 Global Findex wave, with fieldwork in 2022–2023. About 3.3 million is what a 2024 secondary source calls “active savers” in microfinance in 2023 — a count that has not been deduplicated into unique people. And 1,062,441 active bank accounts and 375,252 active e-wallet accounts are the FMIIP project's baselines for January 2025 — accounts, not people. Separately, CBY-Aden reports 5,202,019 accounts for the first half of 2025: a different unit, universe and date from the active bank accounts in the project's baseline, and no ratio between them is published or implied. These figures measure different things, for different populations and dates, from different kinds of evidence. They cannot be added, subtracted, ranked or converted into one another, and no population total is used here to turn the counts into shares. For these figures, “not comparable” is the correct result.
